func (rc *readCounter) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
	n, err := rc.reader.Read(p)

package paasio

import (
	"io"
	"sync"

// readCounter wraps an io.Reader and records how many bytes have been read
// and how many Read calls have been made.
type readCounter struct {
	io.Reader
	mu   sync.Mutex
	n    int64
	nops int
}

// writeCounter wraps an io.Writer and records how many bytes have been written
// and how many Write calls have been made.
type writeCounter struct {
	io.Writer
	mu   sync.Mutex
	n    int64
	nops int
}

// readWriteCounter combines a readCounter and a writeCounter so that it
// satisfies the ReadWriteCounter interface.
type readWriteCounter struct {
	*readCounter
	*writeCounter
}

func NewWriteCounter(writer io.Writer) WriteCounter {
	return &writeCounter{Writer: writer}
}

func NewReadCounter(reader io.Reader) ReadCounter {
	return &readCounter{Reader: reader}
}

	return &readWriteCounter{

}

## What I implemented in `paasio.go`

Per the spec (`.docs/instructions.md`), the package now provides wrappers that report IO statistics — total bytes and total operation counts:

- **`readCounter`** — wraps an `io.Reader`, embedding it and adding a `sync.Mutex`-guarded byte count (`n`) and call count (`nops`). `Read` delegates to the wrapped reader, then records the result under the lock; `ReadCount` returns both under the lock.
- **`writeCounter`** — same design for `io.Writer` / `Write` / `WriteCount`.
- **`readWriteCounter`** — a new type (required by the spec comment) that satisfies `ReadWriteCounter` by combining a `readCounter` and `writeCounter` over the same `io.ReadWriter`, with explicit forwarding methods so both counters work independently.

Key design points:
- Byte counts are only accumulated for successful calls (`err == nil`), matching the interface docs' "bytes successfully read/written"; operation counts increment on every call.
- Both counters are updated atomically under a single mutex, which is what makes the `ReadCount`/`WriteCount` consistency tests (concurrent `Read` + `ReadCount` goroutines) pass race-free.

`paasio_test.go` and `interface.go` were left untouched, and no new files were created.
